short_description: Consumer-facing physical trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to waist circumference tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing physical trait with workable raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited waist-size tendency and current measured waist circumference for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with waist circumference tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Waist circumference tendency is presented here as a cautious panel-relative body-size signal, not as a direct tape-measure readout of your current waist measurement. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct waist measurement, or medical advice about abdominal size.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Real-world waist circumference depends strongly on sex, age, hormones, nutrition, training, pregnancy history, illness, and current body composition, so this should not be treated as a precise measurement of present-day body size.
Waist circumference is only one anthropometric measure and should not be treated as a diagnosis or a complete summary of metabolic health.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
